roles.title: Mechanical Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A mechanically viable robot subsystem.
roles.guideScope: Mechanisms, structures, packaging, tolerances, load analysis, prototypes and design for manufacture.
roles.boundary: Owns the product design; manufacturing engineering owns repeatable production of it. Actuator design is an initial specialization rather than a separate launch guide.

salaryExamples.title: Mechanical Design Engineer - Hands Thermal Systems

roles.title: Electrical Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Working robot electronics and electrical architecture.
roles.guideScope: Mixed-signal boards, sensing interfaces, power distribution, electrical integration and board bring-up.
roles.boundary: Circuit and board design, distinguished from embedded software. Specialist power/charging roles can be expanded later.

postingExamples.title: Senior Electrical Engineer, Reserve and Backup Power

roles.title: Embedded Software Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Reliable software close to the robot hardware.
roles.guideScope: Microcontrollers, firmware, real-time operating systems, peripheral drivers, communication and hardware bring-up.
roles.boundary: The guide centers on device-level timing and hardware interaction. Application middleware and distributed robot runtime belong in the platform guide.

salaryExamples.title: C++ Embedded Software Engineer - Drone Stack

postingExamples.title: Flight Software Engineer, Embedded C/C++, Air Dominance & Strike

roles.title: Manufacturing Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A repeatable process for producing robots at scale.
roles.guideScope: Assembly process definition, fixtures, work instructions, production validation, yield, new-product introduction and ramp.
roles.boundary: Building the robot product at scale; integrating a robot into a customer factory is a different guide.

roles.title: Hardware Test Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Evidence that physical hardware meets its requirements.
roles.guideScope: Instrumented benches and fixtures, component characterization, environmental/lifetime testing and failure investigations.
roles.boundary: Qualifies physical components and assemblies. System V&V centers on autonomy behavior, scenarios and release evidence. Both can use hardware-in-the-loop.

roles.title: Robot Learning Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A trained policy that performs a physical task.
roles.guideScope: Reinforcement learning, imitation learning, vision-language-action models, experiments, policy evaluation and transfer to robots.
roles.boundary: RL, imitation learning and VLA are initially methods/specializations within this guide. Work can overlap planning and control; classify by the primary responsibility.

postingExamples.title: Reinforcement Learning Engineer, Whole Body Control

roles.title: Perception Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A useful interpretation of the robot’s surroundings.
roles.guideScope: Object/human detection, tracking, scene understanding, sensor fusion and production perception models.
roles.boundary: Computer vision is an initial specialization. Scene/object understanding is the center; robot pose estimation and mapping have their own guide. Some employers combine them.

postingExamples.title: Senior AI Software Engineer, Perception
locations: Hybrid- Any Office (Fremont, CA, Salem, OR, or Pittsburgh, PA)

roles.title: Motion Planning Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A feasible path, trajectory or action sequence.
roles.guideScope: Collision avoidance, trajectory optimization, behavior/decision planning, constraints and scenario evaluation.
roles.boundary: Choosing intended motion; the controls guide centers on executing and stabilizing that motion. Broad navigation titles require description-level classification.

salaryExamples.title: Autonomy Engineer- Behavior and Motion Planning (R6007)

roles.title: Robotics Controls Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Stable and accurate physical motion.
roles.guideScope: Robot dynamics, feedback control, system identification, controller tuning, joint/whole-body control and hardware experiments.
roles.boundary: Robot dynamics and feedback, differentiated from PLC-based industrial sequencing in Integration & Operations. Learned control also connects to the learning guide.

salaryExamples.title: Software Engineer: Robotics Controls
salaryExamples.location: San Francisco Bay Area (San Mateo) or Boston (Somerville)

roles.title: Localization & Mapping Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: An estimate of robot pose and a usable spatial map.
roles.guideScope: State estimation, visual-inertial systems, SLAM, calibration, sensor fusion and geometric optimization.
roles.boundary: A distinct estimation and geometry pathway even though perception teams may own it organizationally. Avoid making separate launch guides for SLAM and localization.

salaryExamples.title: Software Engineer - Onboard Maps and State Estimation
Senior Principal Engineer, GNC & State Estimation (R6233)

postingExamples.title: Atlas Research Engineer, SLAM & Spatial AI
Robotics AI Engineer – Calibration, Localization, and Mapping

roles.title: Simulation Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A virtual environment that represents relevant physical behavior.
roles.guideScope: Physics and sensor simulation, scene creation, simulator software, synthetic experience and sim-to-real fidelity.
roles.boundary: Digital twin work is included as an initial specialization. Connected industrial twins can become a separate later guide when scope and audience warrant it. Simulation engineers build the environment; V&V engineers use environments and real robots to establish acceptance evidence.

salaryExamples.title: Research Engineer - Robotic Hardware, Simulation and Data
Senior Robotics Software Engineer, Simulation & Evaluation

roles.title: Robotics Platform Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A reusable software foundation for operating robots.
roles.guideScope: Robot middleware, runtime interfaces, on-robot services, edge/cloud connectivity, updates, observability and developer tooling.
roles.boundary: Shared application/runtime systems rather than autonomy algorithms, low-level microcontroller firmware or ML training infrastructure. Broad infrastructure titles need body-level interpretation.

salaryExamples.title: Senior Software Engineer - Robot Software Infrastructure

roles.title: Robotics Data Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Training-ready and traceable robot datasets.
roles.guideScope: Multimodal recording, synchronization, episode schemas, quality checks, curation, splits, versioning and synthetic-data integration.
roles.boundary: Owns the usable data supply. ML infrastructure owns the systems that execute training and evaluation efficiently. Smaller employers combine both.

salaryExamples.title: Staff Data & Analytics Engineer, Domain Enablement (R6112)

postingExamples.title: Robotics Data Engineer (m/f/d) Data Generation & Curation
Senior Software Engineer, Perception Data Infrastructure

roles.title: Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Reliable and efficient systems for training and evaluating models.
roles.guideScope: Distributed training, GPU utilization, orchestration, experimentation infrastructure, performance profiling and model lifecycle tooling.
searchVariants: Software Engineer, AI Training and Infrastructure
roles.boundary: Distinct from choosing learning algorithms and from producing datasets. GPU systems engineering is a deeper adjacent specialization for a later guide.

salaryExamples.title: Research Member of Technical Staff- Training Systems
Senior/Staff Software Engineer, ML Inference Optimization

postingExamples.title: Software Engineer, AI Training and Infrastructure

roles.title: Verification & Validation Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Evidence that robot capabilities satisfy defined system requirements.
roles.guideScope: Scenario suites, acceptance metrics, simulation/HIL/real-robot tests, regression infrastructure and reproducible failure analysis.
roles.boundary: System behavior and release qualification, differentiated from component hardware characterization and from safety-case ownership. This guide lives here because of its test infrastructure focus; work crosses all categories.

roles.title: Systems Integration Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A robot solution that meets an application’s end-to-end requirements.
roles.guideScope: Hardware/software/model integration, workflow and interface configuration, throughput tuning, commissioning and customer/site acceptance.
roles.boundary: Integration is a broad title. Include application/site performance work; exclude pure product electronics testing or middleware bring-up from this guide’s core. Field service may support deployments but centers on uptime after handover.

roles.title: Industrial Automation Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Control logic connecting intelligent robots to industrial equipment.
roles.guideScope: PLC programming, HMI, industrial networks, machine interfaces, interlocks, sequencing and cell commissioning.
roles.boundary: Programmable logic controllers and cell/equipment coordination, differentiated from feedback robot dynamics. FieldAI’s Automation Engineer is instead an ML deployment role and must not be used as PLC evidence.

roles.title: Systems Safety Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: A defensible safety argument and system safety requirements.
roles.guideScope: Hazard analysis, risk assessment, safety requirements/mechanisms, functional safety and safety-case evidence.
roles.boundary: Safety engineering is broader than a final deployment check. This navigation category is its home, but safety work spans design through operation. V&V supplies evidence against requirements; safety engineering defines and argues acceptable risk.

salaryExamples.title: Senior System Safety Engineer- Robot Stability

postingExamples.title: Sensing and Perception System Safety Engineer

roles.title: Field Service Engineer
roles.ownedOutput: Reliable operation restored and maintained at deployed sites.
roles.guideScope: Diagnostics, repairs, preventive maintenance, upgrades, spares, service documentation and feedback to product engineering.
roles.boundary: Use technician and engineer variants as relevant search routes where duties align, without claiming identical credentials or scope everywhere. Initial installation roles may instead belong in integration.

postingExamples.title: Robot Service Engineer - Data Collection (m/f/d) Fixed-term 18 months

roles.title: Robot Operations Specialist
roles.ownedOutput: A successfully executed and documented robot mission or shift.
roles.guideScope: Robot operation, deployment support, intervention, checklists, behavior observation, incident logging and operational feedback.
roles.boundary: Operating robots differs from repairing them or building fleet software. Data-collection-only teleoperation can be a related separate specialization rather than an automatic alias.

salaryExamples.title: Senior V-BAT Air Vehicle Operator, Demonstration (R5505)

methodology.baseline: 75 manually coded robot-learning postings from October 31, 2026; the expanded study spans 20 roles.
methodology.unit: Distinct listed advertisement / requisition where observable; not individual hires.
methodology.primaryRolePolicy: Exactly one primary family per included posting. Other candidate matches and ambiguity remain available in SQLite.
methodology.deduplication: Same employer/provider/internal job ID; then identical normalized title and full description. Locations and source IDs/URLs are merged. No fuzzy deduplication silently applied.
methodology.roleReview: Analyst-reviewed where source hash or unchanged prior full text supports the decision; otherwise title-and-work deterministic screening. Ambiguous assignments excluded from headline counts.
methodology.skillReview: Machine-coded section/clause evidence, strongest state once per posting/concept. Exact evidence and match offsets retained. No claim all records were manually coded.
methodology.skillsDenominator: All included postings in the selected role; additionally employer presence and equal-employer mean mention rates are retained.
methodology.educationExperience: Preserved conditional clauses; no automatic universal degree or years requirement inferred.
methodology.compensation: Official structured salary fields normalized where present; textual clauses retained separately. No mixed-currency or total-compensation market estimate.

coverageBandThresholds.thin-sample: Below either limited threshold. These are sample-size labels, not accuracy estimates.

methodology.collection: Public employer ATS feeds and public Workday search/detail endpoints. No aggregator counts used. Workday search POST is a read-only query.
methodology.coverage: See collection.json and employers.csv for source status, keyword scope, incomplete indexes and failures. Missing is unknown, not zero.
methodology.historicalPolicy: Keep dated snapshots; same-date explicit refresh archives prior raw metadata and response. Do not infer trends from the earlier narrow study.
limitations: Counts describe deduplicated published advertisements in tracked employer boards, not hires, headcount or the entire market.
Every included record has a role assignment; most role assignments and all new skill coding use transparent automated rules. Review before publishing guide claims.
The 750 target applies across all 20 roles. It is not 750 robot-learning jobs or 750 per role.
Employer coverage is purposive and unequal. Missing or failed boards are unknown, not zero.
Required-or-option includes alternatives and examples in required qualification sections; it does not make each named option compulsory.
Unobserved skills may still be needed. Counts measure explicit posting wording.
A single snapshot does not establish hiring growth or new/closed counts. Earlier small studies have different scopes.
English-language public boards dominate; country labels combine supplied metadata and explicit location rules.
